New Media Art Project

Extinction

Display video

inspirations

The project is inspired by the photographic series ‘The Illustrated Book of Disappearing Animals’ by French photographer Yannick Fourier.
The Illustrated Book of Disappearing Animals is a collection of 69 storytelling essays about how these disappearing animals have become extinct as a result of human activity. The author's chronological vignettes, accompanied by photographs, are intended to inform people that the extinction has already begun and that it is urgent to maintain the balance of biodiversity.
Carolina Parakeet Conuropsis carolinensis →extinct in 1918

In his works, the figures of extinct animals stand in black shadows, and the specimens look either lifelike or twisted. Page after page of photographs, either strong or weak, are interpreting the fact that so many creatures have already left this world and will not be seen again because of man's interfering activities.
Therefore, after analysis, I decided to focus on the theme of animal extinction, presenting the appearance of disappeared animals through data, and using digital interactions to illustrate in a ritualistic way ‘how animals are disappearing due to human activities’.

Pre-research

Media

There are three things that need to be established first in the production of a work.
-The form of the interaction
-The animals shown and their forms
-The structure of the projection

Forms of interaction

In addition more extinct animals, which I have interspersed in the soundtrack in the form of grunts, the overall list is as follows.
Mexican Grizzly Bear
Albino dolphin
Oya nectar-sucking bird
Pyrenean mountain goat
Caspian tiger
Caribbean monk seal
Travelling pigeon
North African Antelope
European wildebeest
Dabbling Sparrow
Steller's sea cow
Blue wildebeest

Most of the animal extinctions are affected by human activities to the point of acceleration.

Therefore, in the trigger conditions, I use the leapmotion and the swinging and clenching of the hand as the trigger conditions. Leapmotion means disturbance, i.e. human activity affects the environment in which creatures live. The clenched fist means killing, whereby many creatures are dispersed, then the next, and so on in an endless cycle.

Animal selection

Due to arithmetic limitations, I have chosen several representative extinct animals from the recent modern period.
Dodo
Pocket wolf
Spotted donkey
Carolina Parakeet
Japanese wolf
Bear's deer

model

production process

Since 3d model to point cloud is based on the principle of detecting the number of model points, a high modelling model with a high number of points is required.
Models are built from animal recovery photos.

programming

Due to the interactive theme, the entire presentation of this work is framed by touchdesigner.
Music is played as two separate tracks of soft music + animal calls
The general logic of the programme is as follows:
Idle:
Background particle generation flows → background music connects glow to form a bright and dark star effect
Animal model rotates → barking audio connects noise to form a disturbance effect
When a human hand is detected:
Background particles are attracted → hand position information connects the attracting particles (allegory of humans sucking the survival resources of animals)
When making a fist:
Model point cloud disperses → switch to next model (implies humans killing animals and infinite loop)
